tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. """Signing in to JusPrin from inside the desktop app, by email.

The app talks to allauth's own API for apps (allauth.headless, the "app"
client): it asks for a code and confirms it, or logs in with a password. Only
those views are mounted (urls.py), not the whole API, so nothing else that
allauth.headless serves, such as its sign-up without the website's reCAPTCHA,
becomes reachable. Between steps the app carries allauth's session token. A
finished sign-in ends in what the browser sign-in ends in: an OAuth2 access and
refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application (TokenStrategy).

Two things allauth does not do here. It looks an address up across every
syndicate, so the code request looks it up in the request's syndicate as the
website does (filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate). And it sends no code to an
address without an account, so the code request makes that account first, with
no usable password, as the website's sign-up would; confirming the code marks
the address verified.
"""
from allauth.account import signals
from allauth.account.adapter import get_adapter
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from allauth.account.utils import setup_user_email
from allauth.core import context, ratelimit
from allauth.headless.account import views as headless
from allauth.headless.account.inputs import RequestLoginCodeInput
from allauth.headless.constants import Client
from allauth.headless.tokens.strategies.sessions import SessionTokenStrategy
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from oauth2_provider.models import Application
from oauth2_provider.settings import oauth2_settings
from oauthlib.common import Request as OAuthRequest

from app.accounts import filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate
from app.models import User
from lib.syndicate import syndicate_from_request

SCOPE = 'read write'


class TokenStrategy(SessionTokenStrategy):
    """allauth's session tokens while the app signs in; once signed in, a new
    access and refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application, issued and saved by
    the same django-oauth-toolkit server and validator as its token endpoint."""

    def create_access_token_payload(self, request):
        server = oauth2_settings.OAUTH2_SERVER_CLASS(oauth2_settings.OAUTH2_VALIDATOR_CLASS(),
                                                     **oauth2_settings.server_kwargs)
        oauth_request = OAuthRequest(request.build_absolute_uri(), http_method='POST')
        oauth_request.user = request.user
        oauth_request.client = Application.objects.get(client_id=settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID)
        oauth_request.scopes = SCOPE.split()
        oauth_request.grant_type = 'authorization_code'
        token = server.default_token_type.create_token(oauth_request, refresh_token=True)
        server.request_validator.save_bearer_token(token, oauth_request)
        return token


class SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput(RequestLoginCodeInput):
    def clean_email(self):
        # RequestLoginCodeForm.clean_email, with the account looked up in the
        # request's syndicate and an inactive one refused rather than
        # passed over, so no second account is made beside it.
        email = self.cleaned_data['email']
        if not email:
            return email
        request = context.request
        if not ratelimit.consume(request, action='request_login_code', key=email.lower()):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('too_many_login_attempts')
        users = filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate(email, syndicate_from_request(request), prefer_verified=True)
        if users and not any(user.is_active for user in users):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('account_inactive')
        active = [user for user in users if user.is_active]
        self._user = active[0] if active else None
        return email


class RequestLoginCodeView(headless.RequestLoginCodeView):
    input_class = SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput

    def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.input._user is None:
            self.input._user = _new_account(request, self.input.cleaned_data['email'])
        return super().post(request, *args, **kwargs)


def _new_account(request, email: str):
    """Makes the account for an address that has none, as the website's sign-up
    does (the account adapter, then the address as an unverified primary
    EmailAddress), with no usable password. Confirming the code verifies the
    address."""
    adapter = get_adapter(request)
    with transaction.atomic():
        user = adapter.new_user(request)
        user.email = email
        user.syndicate = syndicate_from_request(request)
        adapter.populate_username(request, user)
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        setup_user_email(request, user, [EmailAddress(email=email)])
    signals.user_signed_up.send(sender=User, request=request, user=user)
    return user


request_code = RequestLoginCodeView.as_api_view(client=Client.APP)
confirm_code = headless.ConfirmLoginCodeView.as_api_view(client=Client.APP)
login = headless.LoginView.as_api_view(client=Client.APP)

from django.conf import settings
import logging
import requests
from django.db import models
from django import forms
from django.forms import ModelForm, Form, CharField, ChoiceField, Textarea, HiddenInput, BooleanField, ValidationError
from allauth.account.forms import SignupForm, LoginForm, AddEmailForm
import allauth.account.views
import phonenumbers
from pushbullet import Pushbullet, PushbulletError

from .widgets import CustomRadioSelectWidget
from .models import *
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _

from allauth.account.forms import ResetPasswordForm
from allauth.account.adapter import get_adapter
from app.accounts import filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate
from lib.syndicate import syndicate_from_request


LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class SocialAccountAwareLoginForm(LoginForm):
    no_password_yet: bool = False

    def clean(self):
        try:
            return super(SocialAccountAwareLoginForm, self).clean()
        except forms.ValidationError as err:
            if err.message == self.error_messages['email_password_mismatch']:
                email = self.user_credentials().get('email', None)
                if email is not None:
                    users = filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate(email, syndicate_from_request(self.request))
                    if any(not user.has_usable_password() and user.socialaccount_set.exists() for user in users):
                        self.no_password_yet = True
            raise err
    error_messages = {
        'email_password_mismatch': _("Invalid email or password."),
    }


class RecaptchaSignupForm(SignupForm):
    recaptcha_token = CharField(required=True)

    def clean(self):
        super().clean()

        # captcha verification
        recaptcha_token = self.cleaned_data.get('recaptcha_token')
        if not recaptcha_token:
            raise ValidationError('ReCAPTCHA is invalid.')

        data = {
            'response': recaptcha_token,
            'secret': settings.RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY
        }
        response = requests.post('https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify', data=data)

        if response.status_code == requests.codes.ok:
            if response.json()['success'] and response.json()['action'] == 'signup_form':
                LOGGER.debug('Captcha valid for user={}'.format(self.cleaned_data.get('email')))
            else:
                LOGGER.warn('Captcha invalid for user={}'.format(self.cleaned_data.get('email')))
                raise ValidationError('ReCAPTCHA is invalid.')
        else:
            LOGGER.error('Cannot validate reCAPTCHA for user={}'.format(self.cleaned_data.get('email')))

        return self.cleaned_data

class SyndicateSpecificResetPasswordForm(ResetPasswordForm):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.request = kwargs.pop('request', None)
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    def clean_email(self):
        email = self.cleaned_data["email"]
        email = get_adapter().clean_email(email)
        syndicate = syndicate_from_request(self.request)
        self.users = filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate(email, syndicate, is_active=True, prefer_verified=True)
        if not self.users:
            raise get_adapter().validation_error("unknown_email")
        return self.cleaned_data["email"]

class SyndicateSpecificAddEmailForm(AddEmailForm):
    def clean_email(self):
        email = self.cleaned_data['email']
        syndicate = self.user.syndicate  # Assuming the user has a syndicate attribute

        # Check if a user with this email already exists in the same syndicate
        if filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate(email, syndicate):
            raise forms.ValidationError(_("A user is already registered with this email address."))

        return email

from . import sign_in, views, web
from .app_version import supported_app
from .gateway import GatewayEndpoint

# BEFORE PRODUCTION: JusPrin may get a domain of its own instead of
# app.obico.io. These endpoints, the OAuth sign-in pages the desktop app opens

"""Signing in to JusPrin from inside the desktop app, by email.

The app talks to allauth's own API for apps (allauth.headless, the "app"
client): it asks for a code and confirms it, or logs in with a password. Only
those views are mounted (urls.py), not the whole API, so nothing else that
allauth.headless serves, such as its sign-up without the website's reCAPTCHA,
becomes reachable. Between steps the app carries allauth's session token. A
finished sign-in ends in what the browser sign-in ends in: an OAuth2 access and
refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application (TokenStrategy).

Two things allauth does not do here. It looks an address up across every
syndicate, so the code request looks it up in the request's syndicate as the
website does (filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate). And it sends no code to an
address without an account, so the code request makes that account first, with
no usable password, as the website's sign-up would; confirming the code marks
the address verified.
"""
from allauth.account import signals
from allauth.account.adapter import get_adapter
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from allauth.account.utils import setup_user_email
from allauth.core import context, ratelimit
from allauth.headless.account import views as headless
from allauth.headless.account.inputs import RequestLoginCodeInput
from allauth.headless.constants import Client
from allauth.headless.tokens.strategies.sessions import SessionTokenStrategy
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from oauth2_provider.models import Application
from oauth2_provider.settings import oauth2_settings
from oauthlib.common import Request as OAuthRequest

from app.accounts import filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate
from app.models import User
from lib.syndicate import syndicate_from_request

SCOPE = 'read write'


class TokenStrategy(SessionTokenStrategy):
    """allauth's session tokens while the app signs in; once signed in, a new
    access and refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application, issued and saved by
    the same django-oauth-toolkit server and validator as its token endpoint."""

    def create_access_token_payload(self, request):
        server = oauth2_settings.OAUTH2_SERVER_CLASS(oauth2_settings.OAUTH2_VALIDATOR_CLASS(),
                                                     **oauth2_settings.server_kwargs)
        oauth_request = OAuthRequest(request.build_absolute_uri(), http_method='POST')
        oauth_request.user = request.user
        oauth_request.client = Application.objects.get(client_id=settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID)
        oauth_request.scopes = SCOPE.split()
        oauth_request.grant_type = 'authorization_code'
        token = server.default_token_type.create_token(oauth_request, refresh_token=True)
        server.request_validator.save_bearer_token(token, oauth_request)
        return token


class SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput(RequestLoginCodeInput):
    def clean_email(self):
        # RequestLoginCodeForm.clean_email, with the account looked up in the
        # request's syndicate and an inactive one refused rather than
        # passed over, so no second account is made beside it.
        email = self.cleaned_data['email']
        if not email:
            return email
        request = context.request
        if not ratelimit.consume(request, action='request_login_code', key=email.lower()):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('too_many_login_attempts')
        users = filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate(email, syndicate_from_request(request), prefer_verified=True)
        if users and not any(user.is_active for user in users):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('account_inactive')
        active = [user for user in users if user.is_active]
        self._user = active[0] if active else None
        return email

    input_class = SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput

    def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.input._user is None:

        return super().post(request, *args, **kwargs)

    adapter = get_adapter(request)

        user.email = email
        user.syndicate = syndicate_from_request(request)
        adapter.populate_username(request, user)
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        setup_user_email(request, user, [EmailAddress(email=email)])
    signals.user_signed_up.send(sender=User, request=request, user=user)
    return user

def set_up(*args):
    call_command('set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate', *args, stdout=StringIO())
    # Django caches a host's site; a cached one from an earlier test's rows
    # would point at a site this test's database does not have.
    Site.objects.clear_cache()


def setUpModule():
    # The migration that made syndicates inserts base with id 1 and leaves the
    # id sequence at 1, so the first syndicate a test database makes by itself
    # would get id 1 too. Servers made syndicates since, so theirs moved on.
    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
        for sql in connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql(no_style(), [Syndicate]):
            cursor.execute(sql)


class SetUpCommandTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        self.obico_site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})
        self.base.sites.add(self.obico_site)

    def test_the_site_is_jusprins_alone(self):
        set_up(HOST)
        site = Site.objects.get(domain=HOST)
        # Saving a new site added it to the first syndicate; the command took it out.
        self.assertEqual([s.name for s in site.syndicates.all()], ['jusprinv2'])
        self.assertIn(self.obico_site, self.base.sites.all())

    def test_running_again_changes_nothing(self):
        set_up(HOST)
        set_up(HOST)
        self.assertEqual(Syndicate.objects.filter(name='jusprinv2').count(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(Site.objects.filter(domain=HOST).count(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(Syndicate.objects.get(name='jusprinv2').sites.count(), 1)

"""JusPrin as a syndicate of its own: the set-up command, and a sign-in through
JusPrin's host making a JusPrin account beside the person's Obico one."""
import json
import uuid
from io import StringIO

from allauth.socialaccount.models import SocialApp
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.contrib.staticfiles import finders
from django.core import mail
from django.core.management import CommandError, call_command
from django.core.management.color import no_style
from django.db import connection
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from oauth2_provider.models import Application

from app.models import Syndicate, User
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan

EMAIL = 'alex@example.com'
HOST = 'jusprin.testserver'


def set_up(*args):
    call_command('set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate', *args, stdout=StringIO())
    # Django caches a host's site; a cached one from an earlier test's rows
    # would point at a site this test's database does not have.
    Site.objects.clear_cache()


def setUpModule():
    # The migration that made syndicates inserts base with id 1 and leaves the
    # id sequence at 1, so the first syndicate a test database makes by itself
    # would get id 1 too. Servers made syndicates since, so theirs moved on.
    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
        for sql in connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql(no_style(), [Syndicate]):
            cursor.execute(sql)


class SetUpCommandTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        self.obico_site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})
        self.base.sites.add(self.obico_site)

    def test_the_site_is_jusprins_alone(self):
        set_up(HOST)
        site = Site.objects.get(domain=HOST)
        # Saving a new site added it to the first syndicate; the command took it out.
        self.assertEqual([s.name for s in site.syndicates.all()], ['jusprinv2'])
        self.assertIn(self.obico_site, self.base.sites.all())

    def test_running_again_changes_nothing(self):
        set_up(HOST)
        set_up(HOST)
        self.assertEqual(Syndicate.objects.filter(name='jusprinv2').count(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(Site.objects.filter(domain=HOST).count(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(Syndicate.objects.get(name='jusprinv2').sites.count(), 1)

    def test_google_sign_in_from_obicos_host(self):
        google = SocialApp.objects.create(provider='google', name='Google', client_id='id', secret='secret')
        google.sites.add(self.obico_site)
        set_up(HOST, '--google-from', 'testserver')
        self.assertEqual(set(google.sites.values_list('domain', flat=True)), {'testserver', HOST})

    def test_a_host_without_one_google_app_is_refused(self):
        with self.assertRaises(CommandError):
            set_up(HOST, '--google-from', 'testserver')

        response = self.client.post('/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/request', json.dumps({'email': EMAIL}),

        for path in ('jusprinv2/img/favicon.png', settings.SYNDICATES['jusprinv2']['logo_full']):

from django.contrib.sites.shortcuts import get_current_site
from app.models.syndicate_models import Syndicate
from config.settings import SYNDICATES, SITE_USES_HTTPS
import re

def syndicate_from_request(request):
    # 1. user's account syndicate has the highest priority. But I wouldn't be surprised if we later find edge cases that invalidate this rule.
    if request.user.is_authenticated:
      return request.user.syndicate

    # 2. per-request syndicate comes next.
    syndicate_header = request.META.get('HTTP_X_OBICO_SYNDICATE', None)
    if syndicate_header:
      return Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_header)

    # 3. site syndicate is the default.
    return get_current_site(request).syndicates.first()


def settings_for_syndicate(syndicate_name):
    return SYNDICATES[syndicate_name]


SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE = {}

def build_full_url_for_syndicate(url, syndicate_name):
    global SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE
    if syndicate_name not in SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE:
        SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name] = Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_name).sites.first().domain

    domain_name = SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name]

    protocol = 'https://' if SITE_USES_HTTPS else 'http://'
    normalized_url = re.sub(r'^/', '', url)
    return '{}{}/{}'.format(protocol, domain_name, normalized_url)

content.content:
=================== 81efc6fd43
81efc6fd43 2026-11-03
Let the JusPrin app sign in by email, with a code or a password

The desktop app's sign-in door gains an email field next to the browser
sign-in. Four endpoints under ent/jusprin/v2/auth/ serve it:

- email: answers "password" when an active account in the request's
  syndicate has that address and a password its owner set, else emails a
  six-digit code and answers "code".
- code: signs in with the emailed code, making the account for a new
  address (no usable password) and marking the address verified.
- password: signs in with the account's password.
- resend: emails a new code, also for "Email me a code instead".

All four end in a new access and refresh token for the JusPrin2 OAuth
application, as the browser sign-in does, so the app checks and stores the
token the same way. Codes live ten minutes, are used once, allow five tries
and are kept as an HMAC in Redis. Rate limits: 5 codes per address and 20
per client IP per hour, 10 password tries per address per hour.

Choices the brief did not settle:
- An account with a Google sign-in gets a code, not the password step:
  SocialAccountAdapter gives those accounts a random password nobody knows.
- One address can own several accounts in a syndicate that differ only in
  letter case. The most recently signed-in active one is chosen, then the
  newest. The password is checked on that account directly, because
  SyndicateSpecificBackend raises on duplicates.
- A code for an address whose only account is deactivated is refused with
  account_inactive (403) and makes no new account.
- Errors use the gateway's existing body shape, with tries_left beside it.

Tested: jusprin.v2 155 tests pass (23 new) in a local compose stack.
Removing the Google rule or the duplicate ordering fails four of the new
tests.

=================== aa70569e4f
aa70569e4f 2026-11-03
Build JusPrin's email sign-in on allauth and django-oauth-toolkit

The four in-app sign-in endpoints had their own account lookup, sign-up,
password check, rate limits and token minting. They now use what the website
already runs:

- Accounts are found as SyndicateSpecificBackend finds them, made through the
  allauth account adapter with the user_signed_up signal, and their address
  is recorded as verified through allauth's EmailAddress helpers.
- Passwords are checked by the allauth adapter's authenticate(), so the
  website's failed-login limit applies (5 per address in 5 minutes).
- Codes sent are counted by allauth's rate limiter under its
  request_login_code action, set in settings_ent to 5 per address and 20 per
  client IP an hour, the same numbers as before.
- Tokens are created and saved by django-oauth-toolkit's own server and
  validator, as its token endpoint does.

allauth's own login-by-code flow is not used: in 0.63 it looks addresses up
across all syndicates, makes no account for a new address, keeps the code in
the browser session, and enabling it changes the website's login page. The
code store (an HMAC in Redis, ten minutes, five tries, used once) stays.

Behavior that changes: two accounts in one syndicate whose addresses differ
only in letter case now raise, as the website login does, instead of picking
the most recently used one; a correct password for a deactivated account
answers account_inactive (403) instead of wrong_password.

=================== 17e87ee16e
17e87ee16e 2026-11-03
Serve JusPrin's email sign-in from allauth's API for apps

The app's email sign-in now goes through django-allauth 65's headless API
("app" client) instead of JusPrin's own code store. Only three of its views
are mounted, under ent/jusprin/v2/auth/: code/request, code/confirm and
login. Nothing else allauth.headless serves is reachable, so its sign-up
without the website's reCAPTCHA stays off.

Two things allauth does not do here, added in sign_in.py:
- The code request looks the address up in the request's syndicate, as the
  website does, with filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate from obico-server.
- An address with no account gets one when the code is asked for, made the
  way the website's sign-up makes it, with no usable password; confirming
  the code marks the address verified. An inactive account is refused.

A finished sign-in returns an OAuth2 access and refresh token for the
JusPrin 2 application, minted by django-oauth-toolkit's own server and
validator (TokenStrategy). Codes are six digits, ten minutes, five tries;
allauth's rate limits apply. allauth's resend is not mounted: a resent code
keeps the first one's deadline, so the app requests a new code instead.
allauth's website pages for login by code are not served. The code email
keeps JusPrin's wording through allauth's template names.

Needs the obico-server change that adds filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate
(app/accounts.py); that submodule change is not part of this commit.

=================== 1845fe74b9
1845fe74b9 2026-11-05
Give JusPrin 2 a syndicate and brand of its own, the jusprinv2 syndicate

JusPrin 2 signs people in on its own host (jusprinv2.obico.io, staging
jusprinv2-stg.obico.io), with accounts apart from Obico's and apart from
JusPrin v1, whose 'jusprin' brand stays as it was.

set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate creates the jusprinv2 syndicate and the site for
its host, takes that site out of the base syndicate that a new site joins on
save, and attaches the Google sign-in app of an Obico host to it. A request is
then JusPrin 2's by its host, so sign-ups there are JusPrin 2 accounts, with
JusPrin's from-address, and Obico's trial and drips skip them.

SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'] gives the brand its name, logo and links, and its
static folder holds the logo and the favicon every page's layout loads.

jusprin_subscription_status shows the address's account in both syndicates:
a JusPrin v1 subscription is on an Obico account until it is moved by hand to
the person's JusPrin 2 account.

The tests reset the syndicate id sequence first: the migration that made
syndicates inserts base with id 1 and leaves the sequence at 1, so the first
syndicate a test database makes collides with it. A test also looks up the
brand's static files, which tests otherwise serve without the manifest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

the lookup missed the JusPrin 2 account and the server tried to create
another. The fix is in obico-server's filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate;
this test fails with the same IntegrityError without it.

allauth's website pages for login by code are not served. The code email
keeps JusPrin's wording through allauth's template names.

(app/accounts.py); that submodule change is not part of this commit.

731f6947 2026-11-03
Look accounts up by email the same way everywhere, within one syndicate

Each place that found an account by email had its own query. Some read
only EmailAddress rows, one read only User.email, and the login form's
"no password yet" hint looked across every syndicate. An account whose
address had no EmailAddress row was missed by sign-up's duplicate check
and by password reset.

filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate now lives in app/accounts.py and is
allauth's own lookup (EmailAddress rows, then User.email) kept to one
syndicate. Sign-up (web and mobile), add-email, password reset, social
login and the login form's hint all use it. Password reset now takes the
syndicate from syndicate_from_request, so it follows the
X-Obico-Syndicate header as the rest of the site does, and finds only
active accounts, verified addresses first. Social login prefers an
account with a verified address.

tsd-enterprise's in-app email sign-in imports this function.

Look accounts up by email within a syndicate before preferring verified ones

filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate passed prefer_verified to allauth, which
applies it across every syndicate: once the address is verified on any
account, allauth drops all unverified ones before the syndicate filter runs.
An address verified on an Obico account therefore hid the same person's
unverified account in another syndicate, and callers took it for no account
at all. JusPrin 2's email sign-in then tried to create a second account and
failed on the (email, syndicate) unique constraint; the password-reset form
and social sign-in used the same lookup.

The syndicate filter now runs first, and prefer_verified narrows to the
accounts with a verified address within that syndicate.

"""Signing in by email: the allauth API views the app uses, as mounted under
ent/jusprin/v2/auth/, against the test database, an in-memory cache for
allauth's rate limits and Django's in-memory mail outbox."""
import json
import re
import time
import uuid
from unittest import mock

from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core import mail
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application, RefreshToken

from app.models import Syndicate, User

EMAIL = 'alex@example.com'


@override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend')
class SignInTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # allauth counts its rate limits in the default cache; each test starts at zero.
        cache = override_settings(CACHES={'default': {'BACKEND': 'django.core.cache.backends.locmem.LocMemCache',
                                                      'LOCATION': uuid.uuid4().hex}})
        cache.enable()
        self.addCleanup(cache.disable)
        self.syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})
        self.syndicate.sites.add(site)
        site_id = override_settings(SITE_ID=site.id)
        site_id.enable()
        self.addCleanup(site_id.disable)
        self.application = Application.objects.create(
            client_id='JusPrin2', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.session_token = None

    def post(self, endpoint, body=None, ip='203.0.113.1'):
        headers = {'HTTP_X_SESSION_TOKEN': self.session_token} if self.session_token else {}
        response = self.client.post(f'/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/{endpoint}', json.dumps(body or {}),
                                    content_type='application/json', REMOTE_ADDR=ip, **headers)
        token = response.json().get('meta', {}).get('session_token')
        if token:
            self.session_token = token
        return response

    def request_code(self, email=EMAIL, ip='203.0.113.1'):
        self.session_token = None
        return self.post('code/request', {'email': email}, ip=ip)

    def assert_errors(self, response, status, code=None):
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status, response.content)
        if code:
            self.assertIn(code, [error['code'] for error in response.json()['errors']])

    def user(self, email=EMAIL, password=None, syndicate=None, **fields):
        syndicate = syndicate or self.syndicate
        user = User.objects.create(email=email, username=f'{email}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', syndicate=syndicate,
                                   **fields)
        if password:
            user.set_password(password)
        else:
            user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        return user

    def emailed_code(self):
        self.assertEqual(mail.outbox[-1].subject, 'Your JusPrin sign-in code')
        return re.search(r'\b(\d{6})\b', mail.outbox[-1].body).group(1)

    def assert_token_for(self, response, user):
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, response.content)
        meta = response.json()['meta']
        self.assertTrue(meta['is_authenticated'])
        self.assertEqual(meta['token_type'], 'Bearer')
        self.assertEqual(meta['scope'], 'read write')
        access = AccessToken.objects.get(token=meta['access_token'])
        self.assertEqual(access.user, user)
        self.assertEqual(access.application, self.application)
        self.assertTrue(RefreshToken.objects.filter(token=meta['refresh_token'], access_token=access).exists())

    # Asking for a code

    def test_code_for_a_new_address_makes_its_account(self):
        response = self.request_code()
        # allauth's answer: not signed in yet, a code sign-in pending.
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 401, response.content)
        self.assertIn({'id': 'login_by_code', 'is_pending': True}, response.json()['data']['flows'])
        user = User.objects.get(email=EMAIL)
        self.assertEqual(user.username, f'{EMAIL}_{self.syndicate.id}')
        self.assertEqual(user.syndicate, self.syndicate)
        self.assertFalse(user.has_usable_password())
        address = EmailAddress.objects.get(user=user)
        self.assertEqual((address.email, address.primary, address.verified), (EMAIL, True, False))
        self.assertEqual(mail.outbox[0].to, [EMAIL])
        self.assertIn('It expires in 10 minutes.', mail.outbox[0].body)
        self.assertNotIn('http', mail.outbox[0].body)

    def test_code_for_an_existing_account_makes_no_other(self):
        user = self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.request_code(email='Alex@Example.com')
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': self.emailed_code()}), user)
        self.assertEqual(User.objects.filter(email__iexact=EMAIL).count(), 1)

    def test_an_account_in_another_syndicate_is_not_used(self):
        other, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=2, defaults={'name': 'other'})
        elsewhere = self.user(password='REDACTED', syndicate=other)
        self.request_code()
        response = self.post('code/confirm', {'code': self.emailed_code()})
        mine = User.objects.get(email=EMAIL, syndicate=self.syndicate)
        self.assertNotEqual(mine, elsewhere)
        self.assert_token_for(response, mine)

    def test_a_second_code_beside_a_verified_account_in_another_syndicate(self):
        # The first code is never confirmed, so this syndicate's account keeps
        # an unverified address while the other syndicate's is verified.
        other, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=2, defaults={'name': 'other'})
        elsewhere = self.user(syndicate=other)
        EmailAddress.objects.create(user=elsewhere, email=EMAIL, verified=True, primary=True)
        self.request_code()
        self.request_code()
        mine = User.objects.get(email=EMAIL, syndicate=self.syndicate)
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': self.emailed_code()}), mine)

    def test_code_for_a_deactivated_account_makes_no_new_account(self):
        self.user(is_active=False)
        self.assert_errors(self.request_code(), 400, 'account_inactive')
        self.assertEqual(mail.outbox, [])
        self.assertEqual(User.objects.filter(email__iexact=EMAIL).count(), 1)

    def test_not_an_address_is_refused(self):
        self.assert_errors(self.request_code(email='alex'), 400)
        self.assertFalse(User.objects.filter(email='alex').exists())

    def test_codes_are_limited_per_address(self):
        for _ in range(5):
            self.assertEqual(self.request_code().status_code, 401)
        self.assert_errors(self.request_code(), 400, 'too_many_login_attempts')
        self.assertEqual(len(mail.outbox), 5)

    def test_codes_are_limited_per_client(self):
        for index in range(20):
            self.assertEqual(self.request_code(email=f'a{index}@example.com').status_code, 401)
        self.assert_errors(self.request_code(email='b@example.com'), 400, 'too_many_login_attempts')
        self.assertEqual(self.request_code(email='b@example.com', ip='203.0.113.2').status_code, 401)

    # Confirming it

    def test_code_signs_in_and_verifies_the_address(self):
        self.request_code()
        user = User.objects.get(email=EMAIL)
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': self.emailed_code()}), user)
        self.assertTrue(EmailAddress.objects.get(user=user).verified)
        user.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNotNone(user.last_login)

    def test_code_is_six_digits_and_used_once(self):
        self.request_code()
        code = self.emailed_code()
        self.assertRegex(code, r'^\d{6}$')
        self.assertEqual(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': code}).status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': code}).status_code, 409)

    def test_REDACTED_code_five_times_ends_the_code(self):
        self.request_code()
        code = self.emailed_code()
        REDACTED = f'{(int(code) + 1) % 10 ** 6:06d}'
        for _ in range(4):
            self.assert_errors(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': REDACTED}), 400, 'incorrect_code')
        self.assert_errors(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': REDACTED}), 400, 'incorrect_code')
        # Spent: even the right code no longer works.
        self.assertEqual(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': code}).status_code, 409)

    def test_code_expires_after_ten_minutes(self):
        self.request_code()
        code = self.emailed_code()
        later = time.time() + 10 * 60 + 1
        with mock.patch('allauth.account.internal.flows.code_verification.time.time', return_value=later):
            self.assertEqual(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': code}).status_code, 409)

    def test_a_new_code_after_a_spent_one(self):
        # The app asks again rather than resending: a new code gets its own
        # ten minutes and tries.
        self.request_code()
        self.post('code/confirm', {'code': 'x'})
        later = time.time() + 10 * 60 + 1
        with mock.patch('allauth.account.internal.flows.code_verification.time.time', return_value=later):
            self.request_code()
            self.assertEqual(len(mail.outbox), 2)
            self.assertEqual(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': self.emailed_code()}).status_code, 200)

    def test_confirm_without_a_code_request(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.post('code/confirm', {'code': '123456'}).status_code, 409)

    # Password

    def test_password_signs_in(self):
        user = self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('login', {'username': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), user)

    def test_REDACTED_password(self):
        self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.assert_errors(self.post('login', {'username': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), 400)
        self.assert_errors(self.post('login', {'username': 'nobody@example.com', 'password': 'x'}), 400)

    def test_password_of_another_syndicates_account(self):

from django.contrib.sites.shortcuts import get_current_site
from app.models.syndicate_models import Syndicate
from config.settings import SYNDICATES, SITE_USES_HTTPS
import re

def syndicate_from_request(request):
    # 1. user's account syndicate has the highest priority. But I wouldn't be surprised if we later find edge cases that invalidate this rule.
    if request.user.is_authenticated:
      return request.user.syndicate

    # 2. per-request syndicate comes next.
    syndicate_header = request.META.get('HTTP_X_OBICO_SYNDICATE', None)
    if syndicate_header:
      return Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_header)

    # 3. site syndicate is the default.
    return get_current_site(request).syndicates.first()


def settings_for_syndicate(syndicate_name):
    return SYNDICATES[syndicate_name]


SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE = {}

def build_full_url_for_syndicate(url, syndicate_name):
    global SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE
    if syndicate_name not in SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE:
        SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name] = Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_name).sites.first().domain

    domain_name = SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name]

    protocol = 'https://' if SITE_USES_HTTPS else 'http://'
    normalized_url = re.sub(r'^/', '', url)
    return '{}{}/{}'.format(protocol, domain_name, normalized_url)

Let the JusPrin app sign in by email, with a code or a password

The desktop app's sign-in door gains an email field next to the browser
sign-in. Four endpoints under ent/jusprin/v2/auth/ serve it:

- email: answers "password" when an active account in the request's
  syndicate has that address and a password its owner set, else emails a
  six-digit code and answers "code".
- code: signs in with the emailed code, making the account for a new
  address (no usable password) and marking the address verified.
- password: signs in with the account's password.
- resend: emails a new code, also for "Email me a code instead".

All four end in a new access and refresh token for the JusPrin2 OAuth
application, as the browser sign-in does, so the app checks and stores the
token the same way. Codes live ten minutes, are used once, allow five tries
and are kept as an HMAC in Redis. Rate limits: 5 codes per address and 20
per client IP per hour, 10 password tries per address per hour.

Choices the brief did not settle:
- An account with a Google sign-in gets a code, not the password step:
  SocialAccountAdapter gives those accounts a random password nobody knows.
- One address can own several accounts in a syndicate that differ only in
  letter case. The most recently signed-in active one is chosen, then the
  newest. The password is checked on that account directly, because
  SyndicateSpecificBackend raises on duplicates.
- A code for an address whose only account is deactivated is refused with
  account_inactive (403) and makes no new account.
- Errors use the gateway's existing body shape, with tries_left beside it.

Tested: jusprin.v2 155 tests pass (23 new) in a local compose stack.
Removing the Google rule or the duplicate ordering fails four of the new
tests.

Give JusPrin 2 a syndicate and brand of its own, the jusprinv2 syndicate

JusPrin 2 signs people in on its own host (jusprinv2.obico.io, staging
jusprinv2-stg.obico.io), with accounts apart from Obico's and apart from
JusPrin v1, whose 'jusprin' brand stays as it was.

set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate creates the jusprinv2 syndicate and the site for
its host, takes that site out of the base syndicate that a new site joins on
save, and attaches the Google sign-in app of an Obico host to it. A request is
then JusPrin 2's by its host, so sign-ups there are JusPrin 2 accounts, with
JusPrin's from-address, and Obico's trial and drips skip them.

SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'] gives the brand its name, logo and links, and its
static folder holds the logo and the favicon every page's layout loads.

jusprin_subscription_status shows the address's account in both syndicates:
a JusPrin v1 subscription is on an Obico account until it is moved by hand to
the person's JusPrin 2 account.

syndicates inserts base with id 1 and leaves the sequence at 1, so the first
syndicate a test database makes collides with it. A test also looks up the
brand's static files, which tests otherwise serve without the manifest.

JusPrin 2 sign-in: test a second code beside a verified account elsewhere

An address verified on an Obico account and an unfinished JusPrin 2 sign-up
(its address still unverified) made the next code request fail with a 500:
the lookup missed the JusPrin 2 account and the server tried to create
another. The fix is in obico-server's filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate;
this test fails with the same IntegrityError without it.

=================== 731f6947
731f6947 2026-11-03
Look accounts up by email the same way everywhere, within one syndicate

Each place that found an account by email had its own query. Some read
only EmailAddress rows, one read only User.email, and the login form's
"no password yet" hint looked across every syndicate. An account whose
address had no EmailAddress row was missed by sign-up's duplicate check
and by password reset.

filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate now lives in app/accounts.py and is
allauth's own lookup (EmailAddress rows, then User.email) kept to one
syndicate. Sign-up (web and mobile), add-email, password reset, social
login and the login form's hint all use it. Password reset now takes the
syndicate from syndicate_from_request, so it follows the
X-Obico-Syndicate header as the rest of the site does, and finds only
active accounts, verified addresses first. Social login prefers an
account with a verified address.

tsd-enterprise's in-app email sign-in imports this function.

=================== 8f91d6fb
8f91d6fb 2026-11-09
Look accounts up by email within a syndicate before preferring verified ones

filter_users_by_email_and_syndicate passed prefer_verified to allauth, which
applies it across every syndicate: once the address is verified on any
account, allauth drops all unverified ones before the syndicate filter runs.
An address verified on an Obico account therefore hid the same person's
unverified account in another syndicate, and callers took it for no account
at all. JusPrin 2's email sign-in then tried to create a second account and
failed on the (email, syndicate) unique constraint; the password-reset form
and social sign-in used the same lookup.

The syndicate filter now runs first, and prefer_verified narrows to the
accounts with a verified address within that syndicate.

#!/bin/bash -e

RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Trap to catch errors and display in red
trap 'exit_code=$?; trap - ERR; echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Command failed with exit code $exit_code${NC}" >&2; exit $exit_code' ERR

. $HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh

# ── Preflight checks ──

echo "Running preflight checks..."

# Ensure obico-server is on master and push
cd obico-server
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! obico-server is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing obico-server..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push obico-server. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
cd ..

# Ensure tsd-enterprise is on master and push
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! tsd-enterprise is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing tsd-enterprise..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push tsd-enterprise. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Preflight checks passed ✅"

# ── Build ──

cd obico-server/frontend
nvm use
npm ci # for some reason if node_modules folder is missing in the public repo, `npm run build` in the ent repo will fail

if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD --; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
git pull && git checkout master
LAST_PUB_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"
git push

cd ../..
if git diff-index HEAD -- | grep -v obico-server ; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

git pull && git checkout master
LAST_ENT_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"

# Recreate the release branch from master instead of rebasing
git checkout -B release master

cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && npm run build && cd ../..
echo "$LAST_PUB_COMMIT" > web_ent/frontend/builds/last_public_commit.txt
echo "$LAST_ENT_COMMIT" > web_ent/frontend/builds/last_ent_commit.txt
git add web_ent/frontend/builds && git commit -m "Check in built bundles" -m "$LAST_ENT_COMMIT" -m "$LAST_PUB_COMMIT" || true # git return failure when there is nothing to commit
git push -f origin release

git checkout master

#!/bin/bash -e

RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Trap to catch errors and display in red
trap 'exit_code=$?; trap - ERR; echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Command failed with exit code $exit_code${NC}" >&2; exit $exit_code' ERR

. $HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh

# ── Preflight checks ──

echo "Running preflight checks..."

# Ensure obico-server is on master and push
cd obico-server
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! obico-server is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing obico-server..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push obico-server. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
cd ..

# Ensure tsd-enterprise is on master and push
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! tsd-enterprise is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing tsd-enterprise..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push tsd-enterprise. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Preflight checks passed ✅"

# ── Build ──

cd obico-server/frontend
nvm use
npm ci # for some reason if node_modules folder is missing in the public repo, `npm run build` in the ent repo will fail

if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD --; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
git pull && git checkout master
LAST_PUB_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"
git push

cd ../..
if git diff-index HEAD -- | grep -v obico-server ; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

git pull && git checkout master
LAST_ENT_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"

# Recreate the release branch from master instead of rebasing
git checkout -B release master

cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && npm run build && cd ../..
echo "$LAST_PUB_COMMIT" > web_ent/frontend/builds/last_public_commit.txt
echo "$LAST_ENT_COMMIT" > web_ent/frontend/builds/last_ent_commit.txt
git add web_ent/frontend/builds && git commit -m "Check in built bundles" -m "$LAST_ENT_COMMIT" -m "$LAST_PUB_COMMIT" || true # git return failure when there is nothing to commit
git push -f origin release

git checkout master

)

ACCESS_TOKEN_URL = (
    getattr(settings, "SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS", {})
    .get("google", {})
    .get("ACCESS_TOKEN_URL", "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token")
)

AUTHORIZE_URL = (
    getattr(settings, "SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS", {})
    .get("google", {})
    .get("AUTHORIZE_URL", "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth")
)

ID_TOKEN_ISSUER = (
    getattr(settings, "SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS", {})
    .get("google", {})
    .get("ID_TOKEN_ISSUER", "https://accounts.google.com")
)

FETCH_USERINFO = (
    getattr(settings, "SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS", {})
    .get("google", {})
    .get("FETCH_USERINFO", False)
)


def _verify_and_decode(app, credential, verify_signature=True):
    return jwtkit.verify_and_decode(
        credential=credential,
        keys_url=CERTS_URL,
        issuer=ID_TOKEN_ISSUER,
        audience=app.client_id,
        lookup_kid=jwtkit.lookup_kid_pem_x509_certificate,
        verify_signature=verify_signature,
    )


class GoogleOAuth2Adapter(OAuth2Adapter):
    provider_id = "google"
    access_token_url = ACCESS_TOKEN_URL
    authorize_url = AUTHORIZE_URL
    id_token_issuer = ID_TOKEN_ISSUER
    identity_url = IDENTITY_URL
    fetch_userinfo = FETCH_USERINFO

        data = None
        id_token = response.get("id_token")

"""Makes JusPrin 2 a syndicate of its own on this server: the 'jusprinv2'
syndicate, the site for its host, and Google sign-in on that host. Accounts
made through that host are JusPrin 2's, apart from Obico's (the syndicate is
decided by the host, lib/syndicate.py). Its brand is SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'];
the 'jusprin' brand is JusPrin v1's, shown to v1 on Obico's host. Safe to run
again; it changes only what differs.

    python manage.py set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate jusprinv2-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io
"""
from allauth.socialaccount.models import SocialApp
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.db import transaction

from app.models import Syndicate


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Set up the JusPrin 2 syndicate and the site for its host"

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument('domain', help="JusPrin 2's host, as jusprinv2.obico.io")
        parser.add_argument('--google-from', metavar='DOMAIN',
                            help="the host whose Google sign-in app JusPrin 2's host uses too, as app.obico.io")

    @transaction.atomic
    def handle(self, *args, domain, google_from=None, **kwargs):
        syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(name='jusprinv2')
        site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain=domain, defaults={'name': 'JusPrin'})
        # A new site joins the first syndicate (add_site_to_default_syndicate),
        # and a request takes its site's first syndicate, so the site must be
        # JusPrin 2's alone.
        for other in site.syndicates.exclude(id=syndicate.id):
            other.sites.remove(site)
            self.stdout.write(f'Removed {domain} from the {other.name} syndicate')
        syndicate.sites.add(site)
        self.stdout.write(f'{domain} is the jusprinv2 syndicate\'s site')

        if google_from:
            # Google sign-in stores a person's Google ID with the site's id
            # (site_specific_allauth_google_provider), so on this site it makes
            # JusPrin 2 accounts. allauth refuses a site with two Google apps.
            apps = list(SocialApp.objects.filter(provider='google', sites__domain=google_from))
            if len(apps) != 1:
                raise CommandError(f'{google_from} has {len(apps)} Google sign-in apps, not one')
            apps[0].sites.add(site)
            self.stdout.write(f'Google sign-in app "{apps[0].name}" serves {domain}')
